scope: Read-only review of official phase 6 v3 PNG/JSON evidence. Seven changed application images and one new synthetic image were inspected directly; nineteen application images and one synthetic image are byte-identical to previously inspected v2 images. No repository edits or additional browser tests.

qualifications: These images and metadata belong to the exact v3 SHA. All metadata record animations allow. Natural-finish/readiness ordering is established by the source-linked automated tests and counterproofs, not by static pixels alone.

Pink screenshot masks cross some bottom-navigation pixels, including final detail at 375x900/text100 and a thin lower edge at 320x900/text100. Those pixels cannot prove actual application overlap or a fully unobstructed navigation item.
The Next development indicator overlaps part of the first mobile navigation label in some frames; it was not hidden to improve the evidence.
At 844x390/text200 the final confirmation is fully visible while the secondary back action is partly above the header boundary; the capture does not show all actions simultaneously.
The six before-detail captures are the same run before target positioning. They are not evidence of product behavior before a CSS or helper correction.
Physical-device keyboard, assistive technology and manual accessibility acceptance are not established by these emulated static captures.
The two flow screenshots are viewport samples. The uncertain-result frame does not display the entire warning and retry area.
The detail matrix visits a pre-existing fixture after reviewing a new unsaved occurrence. Displayed timestamps across those separate states must not be used as evidence of precision loss.

Nineteen application PNGs and one synthetic PNG are SHA-256 identical to the corresponding v2 files already inspected; that explicit byte comparison supports reuse of the prior pixel observations without claiming a new direct view of every unchanged file.
The successful phase 6 v3 runtime and pixel review do not close the separate phase 7 IHFR 404 failure or establish its cause.
